rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: structural: The requirement asks the review prompt to contain a report template with four sections. That is a content obligation on the prompt itself. It doesn't prescribe a library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation. The only root is `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md`, and it supplies the template.

`section[Requirement group review]/section[Report]/block@fae2e2eda340` is a text code block with all four sections:
- `### Revised text` asks for "every requirement in the group, as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements".
- `### Edits outside the group` asks for the revised text of other requirements that the changes make stale.
- `### Mechanical changes` asks for one line each, listing new full names and added examples.
- `### Design questions` asks for numbered questions.

The paragraph after the block, `section[Report]/paragraph@cb926df5daf1`, covers the case with no design questions.

I found no structural obligation that could be met in a different way while keeping the observable behavior. The clauses describe only what the prompt text contains, and the root contains it.

behavioral: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_gives_a_report_template]` covers all four required sections of the report template.

It takes the `## Report` section of the review prompt with `section(review_prompt(), "## Report")`. The helper `section` stops at the next heading of the same or a higher level outside a code fence, and it collapses whitespace, so line wrapping can't cause a false failure. The test then calls `assert_text_in_order`. That helper requires each phrase to appear after the previous one, and it panics if one is missing.

The obligations map to the assertions as follows:
- **Revised text of every requirement in the group:** the test asserts `### Revised text` and the phrase "as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements". This covers both the complete, pasteable directives and the new split requirements.
- **Revised text of requirements outside the group that the changes affect:** the test asserts `### Edits outside the group` and "revised text of other requirements your changes make stale".
- **Mechanical changes, including new full names and added examples:** the test asserts `### Mechanical changes` and "list new full names and added examples".
- **Design questions:** the test asserts the `### Design questions` heading.

The ordering and scoping assertions would fail if any section were dropped, moved outside `## Report`, or stripped of its described content. The requirement doesn't prescribe the sections' order or the exact wording of their content. The test's phrases are a reasonable check of the stated content, so I found no unresolved ambiguity or gap.

Second assessment `false`: In `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_gives_a_report_template]`, add the phrase "every requirement in the group" to the `assert_text_in_order` list, after "### Revised text" and before "as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements". — The requirement says the first report section holds the revised text of every requirement in the group. The test checks the `### Revised text` heading and the phrase "as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements". It never checks the scope "every requirement in the group", which the real template at `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md` (`## Report`) states. A prompt that said "<the changed requirements, as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements>" would still pass. That prompt would let the reviewer leave out unchanged group members, which breaks the "every" obligation. The other three sections are covered by their headings and descriptive phrases. `section` and `assert_text_in_order` do enforce presence and order within the `## Report` section.
